decisive_items: family history revealed that her uncle and two sisters had sudden cardiac death at a young age
episode of neck and back pain and loss of consciousness
First episode showed complete atrioventricular block with inferior ST-segment elevation
response.rationale: Family history of sudden death and syncope suggest a genetic arrhythmia syndrome; complete AV block with bradycardia is more consistent with a conduction disorder than CPVT (which typically shows polymorphic VT) or Brugada (which has characteristic right precordial ST elevation). Long QT can present with syncope and family history, though QT prolongation is not explicitly stated.

rejected.why: CPVT typically presents with exercise-induced polymorphic VT, not AV block or junctional escape rhythm; no bidirectional VT described.
Brugada syndrome usually shows coved ST elevation in V1-V3, not inferior ST elevation or AV block; no characteristic ECG pattern.
